subject: Civil Engineering
title: Bus Rapid Transit: Buses That Act Like Trains
description: A fast breakdown of Bus Rapid Transit: Buses That Act Like Trains for builders.

hook.text: Curitiba, Brazil, built a metro system using buses — at a fraction of the cost.

buildup.text: BRT uses dedicated lanes, level boarding, and off-board fare collection — like rail.

discovery.text: Articulated buses carry 160 passengers. Bi-articulated ones carry 270 — train capacity.

twist.text: BRT can be built in two years. A metro line takes ten or more — time matters.

climax.text: Bogotá's TransMilenio moves 2.4 million daily — the world's busiest BRT system.

punchline.text: Give buses their own lane and they become a metro on rubber tires.

quiz.question: What makes BRT different from a regular bus service?
options: BRT uses smaller vehicles for faster acceleration
BRT has dedicated lanes, level boarding, and operates like a rail system
BRT runs only during off-peak hours to reduce congestion
